title: Division of 4-Digit by 3-Digit Numbers
seo_title: Grade 6 Division Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Divide at least whole 4-digit by 3-digit numbers.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 6 division worksheets: short division, long division by 2-digit and 3-digit numbers, remainders and problems. 100 questions with memos.
key_big: Estimate how many times the divisor fits.
key_sub: The remainder is smaller than the divisor.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • To divide by a 3-digit number, estimate how many times it fits: 8 064 ÷ 252 → about 8 000 ÷ 250 = 32.
  • Use multiples of the divisor: 252 × 30 = 7 560, then 8 064 − 7 560 = 504 = 252 × 2.
  • The remainder must be smaller than the divisor.
  • Check: answer × divisor + remainder = the number you divided.

Examples

Example

8 064 ÷ 252

252 × 30 = 7 560

8 064 − 7 560 = 504

504 = 252 × 2

Answer: 32

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Big remainderIf the remainder ≥ divisor, divide again.
A missing 03 618 ÷ 18 = 201, not 21.
Ignoring the remainderDecide what the story needs.

faq.q: What does CAPS Grade 6 say about division?
faq.a: Divide at least whole 4-digit by 3-digit numbers.

faq.q: How do I check a division?
faq.a: Multiply the answer by the divisor and add the remainder.
Estimate how many times the divisor fits.

faq.q: When do I round the answer up?
faq.a: When the leftover items still need a place, like taxis for learners.

items.q: 2 028 ÷ 6 = 338. Which calculation checks this answer?
items.e: Multiplication is the inverse of division. 338 × 6 = 2 028, which matches, so the answer is right.

items.q: Use short division to work out 2 134 ÷ 11.
items.e: 2 ÷ 11: 11 does not go into 2, so carry the 2 to make 21; 21 ÷ 11 = 1 r 10, carry the 10 to make 103; 103 ÷ 11 = 9 r 4, carry the 4 to make 44; 44 ÷ 11 = 4. Answer: 194. Check: 194 × 11 = 2 134.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 8 ÷ 12: 12 does not go into 8, so carry the 8 to make 80; 80 ÷ 12 = 6 r 8, carry the 8 to make 81; 81 ÷ 12 = 6 r 9, carry the 9 to make 96; 96 ÷ 12 = 8. Answer: 668. Check: 668 × 12 = 8 016.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 7 ÷ 25: 25 does not go into 7, so carry the 7 to make 73; 73 ÷ 25 = 2 r 23, carry the 23 to make 232; 232 ÷ 25 = 9 r 7, carry the 7 to make 75; 75 ÷ 25 = 3. Answer: 293. Check: 293 × 25 = 7 325.

items.q: Use short division to work out 7 736 ÷ 8.
items.e: 7 ÷ 8: 8 does not go into 7, so carry the 7 to make 77; 77 ÷ 8 = 9 r 5, carry the 5 to make 53; 53 ÷ 8 = 6 r 5, carry the 5 to make 56; 56 ÷ 8 = 7. Answer: 967. Check: 967 × 8 = 7 736.

items.q: Karabo uses short division for 571 ÷ 4. First, 5 ÷ 4 = 1 r 1. What does she divide next?
items.e: 5 ÷ 4 = 1 r 1. The remainder 1 is 1 hundred, which is 10 tens. Write it as a small 1 in front of the 7, so you divide 17 next: 17 ÷ 4 = 4 r 1. The whole answer: 142 r 3.

items.q: Use short division to work out 9 043 ÷ 25.
items.e: 9 ÷ 25: 25 does not go into 9, so carry the 9 to make 90; 90 ÷ 25 = 3 r 15, carry the 15 to make 154; 154 ÷ 25 = 6 r 4, carry the 4 to make 43; 43 ÷ 25 = 1 r 18. Answer: 361 r 18. Check: 361 × 25 + 18 = 9 043.

items.q: Use short division to work out 1 674 ÷ 6.
items.e: 1 ÷ 6: 6 does not go into 1, so carry the 1 to make 16; 16 ÷ 6 = 2 r 4, carry the 4 to make 47; 47 ÷ 6 = 7 r 5, carry the 5 to make 54; 54 ÷ 6 = 9. Answer: 279. Check: 279 × 6 = 1 674.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 2 ÷ 9: 9 does not go into 2, so carry the 2 to make 24; 24 ÷ 9 = 2 r 6, carry the 6 to make 61; 61 ÷ 9 = 6 r 7, carry the 7 to make 71; 71 ÷ 9 = 7 r 8. Answer: 267 r 8. Check: 267 × 9 + 8 = 2 411.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 1 ÷ 3: 3 does not go into 1, so carry the 1 to make 18; 18 ÷ 3 = 6; 1 ÷ 3 = 0 r 1, carry the 1 to make 15; 15 ÷ 3 = 5. Answer: 605. Check: 605 × 3 = 1 815.

items.q: Use short division to work out 7 242 ÷ 6.
items.e: 7 ÷ 6 = 1 r 1, carry the 1 to make 12; 12 ÷ 6 = 2; 4 ÷ 6 = 0 r 4, carry the 4 to make 42; 42 ÷ 6 = 7. Answer: 1 207. Check: 1 207 × 6 = 7 242.

items.q: Use short division to work out 6 465 ÷ 15.
items.e: 6 ÷ 15: 15 does not go into 6, so carry the 6 to make 64; 64 ÷ 15 = 4 r 4, carry the 4 to make 46; 46 ÷ 15 = 3 r 1, carry the 1 to make 15; 15 ÷ 15 = 1. Answer: 431. Check: 431 × 15 = 6 465.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 5 ÷ 4 = 1 r 1, carry the 1 to make 11; 11 ÷ 4 = 2 r 3, carry the 3 to make 36; 36 ÷ 4 = 9. Answer: 129. Check: 129 × 4 = 516.

items.q: Siyabonga uses short division for 832 ÷ 7. First, 8 ÷ 7 = 1 r 1. What does he divide next?
items.e: 8 ÷ 7 = 1 r 1. The remainder 1 is 1 hundred, which is 10 tens. Write it as a small 1 in front of the 3, so you divide 13 next: 13 ÷ 7 = 1 r 6. The whole answer: 118 r 6.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 5 ÷ 11: 11 does not go into 5, so carry the 5 to make 52; 52 ÷ 11 = 4 r 8, carry the 8 to make 80; 80 ÷ 11 = 7 r 3, carry the 3 to make 35; 35 ÷ 11 = 3 r 2. Answer: 473 r 2. Check: 473 × 11 + 2 = 5 205.

items.q: Use short division to work out 8 790 ÷ 7.
items.e: 8 ÷ 7 = 1 r 1, carry the 1 to make 17; 17 ÷ 7 = 2 r 3, carry the 3 to make 39; 39 ÷ 7 = 5 r 4, carry the 4 to make 40; 40 ÷ 7 = 5 r 5. Answer: 1 255 r 5. Check: 1 255 × 7 + 5 = 8 790.

items.q: Use short division to work out 9 036 ÷ 8.
items.e: 9 ÷ 8 = 1 r 1, carry the 1 to make 10; 10 ÷ 8 = 1 r 2, carry the 2 to make 23; 23 ÷ 8 = 2 r 7, carry the 7 to make 76; 76 ÷ 8 = 9 r 4. Answer: 1 129 r 4. Check: 1 129 × 8 + 4 = 9 036.

items.q: Use short division to work out 5 352 ÷ 12.
items.e: 5 ÷ 12: 12 does not go into 5, so carry the 5 to make 53; 53 ÷ 12 = 4 r 5, carry the 5 to make 55; 55 ÷ 12 = 4 r 7, carry the 7 to make 72; 72 ÷ 12 = 6. Answer: 446. Check: 446 × 12 = 5 352.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 5 ÷ 7: 7 does not go into 5, so carry the 5 to make 55; 55 ÷ 7 = 7 r 6, carry the 6 to make 65; 65 ÷ 7 = 9 r 2, carry the 2 to make 21; 21 ÷ 7 = 3. Answer: 793. Check: 793 × 7 = 5 551.

items.q: 3 792 ÷ 12 = 316. Which calculation checks this answer?
items.e: Multiplication is the inverse of division. 316 × 12 = 3 792, which matches, so the answer is right.

items.q: What is the remainder when 959 is divided by 62?
items.e: The question asks for the remainder, not the answer to the division. 9 is less than 62, so start with 95. 95 ÷ 62 = 1: 1 × 62 = 62, 95 − 62 = 33. Bring down 9 to make 339: 339 ÷ 62 = 5: 5 × 62 = 310, 339 − 310 = 29. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 29. Answer: 15 r 29. Check: 15 × 62 + 29 = 959.

items.q: Use long division.
items.e: 8 is less than 35, so start with 86. 86 ÷ 35 = 2: 2 × 35 = 70, 86 − 70 = 16. Bring down 8 to make 168: 168 ÷ 35 = 4: 4 × 35 = 140, 168 − 140 = 28. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 28. Answer: 24 r 28. Check: 24 × 35 + 28 = 868.

items.q: Use long division to work out 773 ÷ 64.
items.e: 7 is less than 64, so start with 77. 77 ÷ 64 = 1: 1 × 64 = 64, 77 − 64 = 13. Bring down 3 to make 133: 133 ÷ 64 = 2: 2 × 64 = 128, 133 − 128 = 5. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 5. Answer: 12 r 5. Check: 12 × 64 + 5 = 773.

items.q: You use long division for 456 ÷ 19. The first step is 45 ÷ 19. Which multiple of 19 do you subtract from 45?
items.e: List the multiples of 19: 19, 38, 57, 76, 95, … The largest one that is not more than 45 is 2 × 19 = 38. 45 − 38 = 7. Then bring down the next digit. The whole answer: 456 ÷ 19 = 24.

items.q: Use long division.
items.e: 9 is less than 51, so start with 91. 91 ÷ 51 = 1: 1 × 51 = 51, 91 − 51 = 40. Bring down 5 to make 405: 405 ÷ 51 = 7: 7 × 51 = 357, 405 − 357 = 48. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 48. Answer: 17 r 48. Check: 17 × 51 + 48 = 915.

items.q: Use long division.
Use long division.
Use long division to work out 493 ÷ 17.
Use long division to work out 990 ÷ 22.
You use long division for 702 ÷ 27. The first step is 70 ÷ 27. Which multiple of 27 do you subtract from 70?
items.e: List the multiples of 27: 27, 54, 81, 108, 135, … The largest one that is not more than 70 is 2 × 27 = 54. 70 − 54 = 16. Then bring down the next digit. The whole answer: 702 ÷ 27 = 26.

items.q: Lindiwe works out 3 886 ÷ 26 = 148 r 38. What mistake did she make?
c: She forgot to bring down a digit
She missed a 0 in the answer
items.e: A remainder must be less than the divisor. 38 is more than 26, so 26 goes in once more: 38 − 26 = 12. The answer is 149 r 12. Check: 149 × 26 + 12 = 3 886.

items.q: How many digits will the answer to 9 692 ÷ 66 have (not counting the remainder)?
items.e: 96 is at least 66, so the answer starts in the hundreds place. 9 692 ÷ 66 = 146 r 56.

items.q: Use long division.
items.e: 9 is less than 88, so start with 98. 98 ÷ 88 = 1: 1 × 88 = 88, 98 − 88 = 10. Bring down 6 to make 106: 106 ÷ 88 = 1: 1 × 88 = 88, 106 − 88 = 18. Bring down 4 to make 184: 184 ÷ 88 = 2: 2 × 88 = 176, 184 − 176 = 8. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 8. Answer: 112 r 8. Check: 112 × 88 + 8 = 9 864.

items.q: Use long division.
Use long division.
items.e: 1 is less than 18, so start with 19. 19 ÷ 18 = 1: 1 × 18 = 18, 19 − 18 = 1. Bring down 4 to make 14: 18 does not go into 14, so write 0 in the answer. Bring down 4 to make 144: 144 ÷ 18 = 8: 8 × 18 = 144, 144 − 144 = 0. Answer: 108. Check: 108 × 18 = 1 944.

items.q: Use long division to work out 1 309 ÷ 17.
Use long division.
items.e: 7 is less than 52, so start with 72. 72 ÷ 52 = 1: 1 × 52 = 52, 72 − 52 = 20. Bring down 7 to make 207: 207 ÷ 52 = 3: 3 × 52 = 156, 207 − 156 = 51. Bring down 3 to make 513: 513 ÷ 52 = 9: 9 × 52 = 468, 513 − 468 = 45. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 45. Answer: 139 r 45. Check: 139 × 52 + 45 = 7 273.

items.q: How many digits will the answer to 6 104 ÷ 82 have (not counting the remainder)?
items.e: 61 is less than 82, so there are no hundreds. The answer starts in the tens place. 6 104 ÷ 82 = 74 r 36.

items.q: Use long division to work out 4 387 ÷ 92.
items.e: 43 is less than 92, so start with 438. 438 ÷ 92 = 4: 4 × 92 = 368, 438 − 368 = 70. Bring down 7 to make 707: 707 ÷ 92 = 7: 7 × 92 = 644, 707 − 644 = 63. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 63. Answer: 47 r 63. Check: 47 × 92 + 63 = 4 387.

items.q: Nomsa works out 1 696 ÷ 16 = 16. What mistake did she make?
c: She missed a 0 in the answer
She divided the wrong way round
items.e: Check: 16 × 16 = 256, not 1 696. Every digit you bring down needs a digit in the answer, even 0. 1 is less than 16, so start with 16. 16 ÷ 16 = 1: 1 × 16 = 16, 16 − 16 = 0. Bring down 9 to make 9: 16 does not go into 9, so write 0 in the answer. Bring down 6 to make 96: 96 ÷ 16 = 6: 6 × 16 = 96, 96 − 96 = 0. Answer: 106. Check: 106 × 16 = 1 696.
108 × 90 = 9 720, with 82 left over. Answer: 90 r 82.

items.q: Work out 1 776 ÷ 25. Give your answer as a decimal.
items.e: 1 776 ÷ 25 = 71 r 1. The remainder 1 out of 25 is 125 = 1 ÷ 25 = 0,04. So the answer is 71,04, not 71,1.

items.q: Work out 4 482 ÷ 20. Give your answer as a decimal.
items.e: 4 482 ÷ 20 = 224 r 2. The remainder 2 out of 20 is 220 = 2 ÷ 20 = 0,1. So the answer is 224,1, not 224,2.

items.q: Lungile works out 4 591 ÷ 8 = 573 r 7 and writes the answer as 573,7. What is the correct decimal answer?
items.e: The remainder 7 is not 0,7. It means 7 out of 8, so it is 78 = 7 ÷ 8 = 0,875. The answer is 573,875.

items.q: Work out 8 734 ÷ 63. Give the remainder as a whole number.
items.e: 8 is less than 63, so start with 87. 87 ÷ 63 = 1: 1 × 63 = 63, 87 − 63 = 24. Bring down 3 to make 243: 243 ÷ 63 = 3: 3 × 63 = 189, 243 − 189 = 54. Bring down 4 to make 544: 544 ÷ 63 = 8: 8 × 63 = 504, 544 − 504 = 40. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 40. Answer: 138 r 40. Check: 138 × 63 + 40 = 8 734.

items.q: Work out 588 ÷ 15. Give your answer as a decimal.
items.e: 588 ÷ 15 = 39 r 3. The remainder 3 out of 15 is 315 = 3 ÷ 15 = 0,2. So the answer is 39,2, not 39,3.

items.q: Work out 1 601 ÷ 26. Give your answer to 1 decimal place.
items.e: 1 601 ÷ 26 = 61 r 15, and 1 601 ÷ 26 = 61,576… (keep dividing: add a decimal point and zeros). The hundredths digit is 7, which is 5 or more, so round the tenths up: 61,6.

items.q: Work out 1 489 ÷ 67. Give the remainder as a whole number.
items.e: 14 is less than 67, so start with 148. 148 ÷ 67 = 2: 2 × 67 = 134, 148 − 134 = 14. Bring down 9 to make 149: 149 ÷ 67 = 2: 2 × 67 = 134, 149 − 134 = 15. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 15. Answer: 22 r 15. Check: 22 × 67 + 15 = 1 489.

items.q: Work out 2 672 ÷ 12. Give your answer as a mixed number in its simplest form.
items.e: 2 672 ÷ 12 = 222 r 8. The remainder 8 is 8 out of 12, so the fraction is 812. Simplify: divide the numerator and the denominator by 4 to get 23. Answer: 222 23.

items.q: Work out 872 ÷ 19. Give your answer as a mixed number.
items.e: 872 ÷ 19 = 45 r 17. The remainder 17 is 17 out of 19, so the fraction is 1719. Answer: 45 1719.

items.q: Work out 4 437 ÷ 25. Give your answer as a decimal.
items.e: 4 437 ÷ 25 = 177 r 12. The remainder 12 out of 25 is 1225 = 12 ÷ 25 = 0,48. So the answer is 177,48, not 177,12.

items.q: Work out 151 ÷ 12. Give your answer as a mixed numeral.
items.e: 1 is less than 12, so start with 15. 15 ÷ 12 = 1: 1 × 12 = 12, 15 − 12 = 3. Bring down 1 to make 31: 31 ÷ 12 = 2: 2 × 12 = 24, 31 − 24 = 7. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 7. So the quotient is 12 r 7. The remainder 7 is 7 out of 12, so it is 712. Answer: 12 712.

items.q: 575 learners are going on a school excursion. Each bus has 46 seats. Ethan works out 575 ÷ 46 = 12 r 23 and says 12 buses are needed. What is the right answer?
items.e: 12 buses only seat 12 × 46 = 552 learners. The other 23 learners still need seats, so Ethan rounded the wrong way. Round up: 13 buses.

items.q: 577 people are coming to the school musical. The chairs are set out in rows of 22. How many rows are needed so everyone has a seat?
items.e: 577 ÷ 22 = 26 r 5. 26 rows hold 26 × 22 = 572 people. 5 people still need a place, so you need 1 more: 27 rows. Round up.

items.q: 81 Grade 6 learners are going to the swimming gala. Each minibus has 12 seats for learners. How many minibuses are needed?
items.e: 81 ÷ 12 = 6 r 9. 6 minibuses hold 6 × 12 = 72 learners. 9 learners still need a place, so you need 1 more: 7 minibuses. Round up.

items.q: A nursery has 787 seedlings. It plants them in trays of 24. 787 ÷ 24 = 32 r 19. To find how many trays are full, what should you do with the remainder?
items.e: A tray with fewer than 24 seedlings is not full, so ignore the remainder. Round down: 32 full trays.

items.q: A farm has 769 eggs. It packs them into trays of 30. How many full trays can it pack?
items.e: 769 ÷ 30 = 25 r 19. The 19 eggs left over are not enough to fill another tray, so ignore the remainder. Round down: 25 trays.

items.q: A school needs 1 493 exercise books for next year. They come in boxes of 36. How many boxes must the school order?
items.e: 1 493 ÷ 36 = 41 r 17. 41 boxes hold 41 × 36 = 1 476 books. The school still needs 17 more books, so it must order 1 more box: 42 boxes. Round up.

items.q: 272 learners sign up for the summer cricket competition. Each team needs exactly 11 players. How many full teams can be made?
items.e: 272 ÷ 11 = 24 r 8. The 8 learners left over are not enough to make another team, so ignore the remainder. Round down: 24 teams.

items.q: 466 learners line up in rows of 24 for the school photo. How many learners are in the last row, which is not full?
items.e: 466 ÷ 24 = 19 r 10. The question asks how many are left over, so the remainder is the answer: 10 learners.

items.q: A bakery makes 371 lamingtons. Each box holds 12 lamingtons. How many boxes can be filled?
items.e: 371 ÷ 12 = 30 r 11. The 11 lamingtons left over are not enough to fill another box, so ignore the remainder. Round down: 30 boxes.

items.q: A rope is 728 cm long. It is cut into 20 equal pieces. How long is each piece?
items.e: Divide: 7 is less than 20, so start with 72. 72 ÷ 20 = 3: 3 × 20 = 60, 72 − 60 = 12. Bring down 8 to make 128: 128 ÷ 20 = 6: 6 × 20 = 120, 128 − 120 = 8. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 8. So 728 ÷ 20 = 36 r 8. Lengths can be split into parts, so write the remainder as a decimal: 820 = 8 ÷ 20 = 0,4. Each piece is 36,4 cm, not 36,8 cm.

items.q: A garden centre has 1 603 bulbs. It packs them in bags of 48 and fills as many bags as it can. How many bulbs are not in a bag?
items.e: Divide: 16 is less than 48, so start with 160. 160 ÷ 48 = 3: 3 × 48 = 144, 160 − 144 = 16. Bring down 3 to make 163: 163 ÷ 48 = 3: 3 × 48 = 144, 163 − 144 = 19. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 19. So 1 603 ÷ 48 = 33 r 19. The question asks how many are left over. That is the remainder: 19 bulbs.

items.q: Fatima has a roll of ribbon 524 cm long. She cuts it into pieces that are each 15 cm long. How many full pieces can she cut?
items.e: Divide: 5 is less than 15, so start with 52. 52 ÷ 15 = 3: 3 × 15 = 45, 52 − 45 = 7. Bring down 4 to make 74: 74 ÷ 15 = 4: 4 × 15 = 60, 74 − 60 = 14. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 14. So 524 ÷ 15 = 34 r 14. The 14 centimetres left over are not enough to cut another piece, so ignore the remainder. The answer is 34 pieces.

items.q: There are 224 people coming to a summer fair lunch. Each table seats 12 people. How many tables are needed so everyone has a seat?
items.e: Divide: 2 is less than 12, so start with 22. 22 ÷ 12 = 1: 1 × 12 = 12, 22 − 12 = 10. Bring down 4 to make 104: 104 ÷ 12 = 8: 8 × 12 = 96, 104 − 96 = 8. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 8. So 224 ÷ 12 = 18 r 8. 18 tables are not enough: 8 people would still need a seat. You need 1 more, so the answer is 19 tables.

items.q: There are 228 children at a soccer tournament. Each team needs exactly 11 players. How many full teams can be made?
items.e: Divide: 2 is less than 11, so start with 22. 22 ÷ 11 = 2: 2 × 11 = 22, 22 − 22 = 0. Bring down 8 to make 8: 11 does not go into 8, so write 0 in the answer. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 8. So 228 ÷ 11 = 20 r 8. The 8 children left over are not enough to make another team, so ignore the remainder. The answer is 20 teams.

items.q: A school is taking 599 learners and adults on a trip to the seaside. Each coach has 53 seats. How many coaches are needed?
items.e: Divide: 5 is less than 53, so start with 59. 59 ÷ 53 = 1: 1 × 53 = 53, 59 − 53 = 6. Bring down 9 to make 69: 69 ÷ 53 = 1: 1 × 53 = 53, 69 − 53 = 16. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 16. So 599 ÷ 53 = 11 r 16. 11 coaches are not enough: 16 people would still need a seat. You need 1 more, so the answer is 12 coaches.

items.q: Zinhle shares 629 stickers equally among 24 learners. Each learner gets as many as possible. How many stickers are left over?
items.e: Divide: 6 is less than 24, so start with 62. 62 ÷ 24 = 2: 2 × 24 = 48, 62 − 48 = 14. Bring down 9 to make 149: 149 ÷ 24 = 6: 6 × 24 = 144, 149 − 144 = 5. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 5. So 629 ÷ 24 = 26 r 5. The question asks how many are left over. That is the remainder: 5 stickers.

items.q: A school orders 2 556 pencils. They come in packs of 12. How many packs does the school order?
items.e: Divide: 2 is less than 12, so start with 25. 25 ÷ 12 = 2: 2 × 12 = 24, 25 − 24 = 1. Bring down 5 to make 15: 15 ÷ 12 = 1: 1 × 12 = 12, 15 − 12 = 3. Bring down 6 to make 36: 36 ÷ 12 = 3: 3 × 12 = 36, 36 − 36 = 0. So 2 556 ÷ 12 = 213. There is no remainder, so the answer is 213 packs.

items.q: Siyabonga is putting 491 photos into an album. Each page holds 16 photos. How many pages does he need?
items.e: Divide: 4 is less than 16, so start with 49. 49 ÷ 16 = 3: 3 × 16 = 48, 49 − 48 = 1. Bring down 1 to make 11: 16 does not go into 11, so write 0 in the answer. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 11. So 491 ÷ 16 = 30 r 11. 30 pages are not enough: 11 photos would still need a page. You need 1 more, so the answer is 31 pages.

items.q: Nadia bakes 86 cakes for a party. They are shared equally between 12 tables. How many cakes does each table get?
items.e: Divide: 8 is less than 12, so start with 86. 86 ÷ 12 = 7: 7 × 12 = 84, 86 − 84 = 2. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 2. So 86 ÷ 12 = 7 r 2. The remainder can be shared too: 2 cakes ÷ 12 = 212 cake. Simplify: 212 = 16. Each gets 7 16 cakes.

items.q: Refilwe works out 5 099 ÷ 24 = 211 r 35. What mistake did she make?
items.e: A remainder must be less than the divisor. 35 is more than 24, so 24 goes in once more: 35 − 24 = 11. The answer is 212 r 11. Check: 212 × 24 + 11 = 5 099.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 4 does not go into 2, so carry the 2 to make 26; 26 ÷ 4 = 6 r 2, carry the 2 to make 21; 21 ÷ 4 = 5 r 1, carry the 1 to make 16; 16 ÷ 4 = 4. Answer: 654. Check: 654 × 4 = 2 616.

items.q: Use long division to work out 455 ÷ 35.
Use long division.
items.e: 5 is less than 33, so start with 50. 50 ÷ 33 = 1: 1 × 33 = 33, 50 − 33 = 17. Bring down 6 to make 176: 176 ÷ 33 = 5: 5 × 33 = 165, 176 − 165 = 11. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 11. Answer: 15 r 11. Check: 15 × 33 + 11 = 506.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 9 ÷ 8 = 1 r 1, carry the 1 to make 16; 16 ÷ 8 = 2; 8 does not go into 2, so write 0 in the quotient and carry the 2 to make 23; 23 ÷ 8 = 2 r 7. Answer: 1 202 r 7. Check: 1 202 × 8 + 7 = 9 623.

items.q: Aisha works out 6 936 ÷ 34 = 24. What mistake did she make?
items.e: Check: 24 × 34 = 816, not 6 936. When 34 does not go into the number, write 0 in the quotient. 6 is less than 34, so start with 69. 69 ÷ 34 = 2: 2 × 34 = 68, 69 − 68 = 1. Bring down 3 to make 13: 34 does not go into 13, so write 0 in the quotient. Bring down 6 to make 136: 136 ÷ 34 = 4: 4 × 34 = 136, 136 − 136 = 0. Answer: 204. Check: 204 × 34 = 6 936.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 9 does not go into 6, so carry the 6 to make 63; 63 ÷ 9 = 7; 9 does not go into 5, so write 0 in the quotient and carry the 5 to make 54; 54 ÷ 9 = 6. Answer: 706. Check: 706 × 9 = 6 354.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for 6 108 ÷ 31?
items.e: Round to numbers that divide easily: 6 108 is about 6 000 and 31 is about 30. 6 000 ÷ 30 = 200. The exact answer is 197 r 1.

items.q: Use long division to work out 1 472 ÷ 23.
Use short division to work out 9 208 ÷ 8.
items.e: 9 ÷ 8 = 1 r 1, carry the 1 to make 12; 12 ÷ 8 = 1 r 4, carry the 4 to make 40; 40 ÷ 8 = 5; 8 ÷ 8 = 1. Answer: 1 151. Check: 1 151 × 8 = 9 208.
